kind.description: meridian for the MC and IC lines, which are straight; horizon for the rising and setting lines, which are not.

phase.description: applying, separating, exact, or indeterminate. Indeterminate is a real answer, not a failure: two natal charts share no timeline, so cross-aspects between them have no direction of travel.

bodies.title: Bodies

Where each body is angular on Earth for this chart's instant.

A physical fact, so the lines do not move when the chart's zodiac changes.

ayanamsa.description: Present only when zodiac is sidereal.

Every contribution that produced the totals is itemised and every weight is
in `profile`, so the number can be audited rather than trusted.

A natal aspect plus an evidence id.

Cross-chart contacts carry one and natal aspects do not, because everything
downstream of synastry -- score contributions, evidence bundles, the report
outline, the timing layer's activation marks -- addresses facts by id.

phase.description: applying, separating, exact, or indeterminate. Indeterminate is a real answer, not a failure: two natal charts share no timeline, so cross-aspects between them have no direction of travel.

chart.description: An ordinary natal chart, because that is what a Davison chart is.

chartRuler.description: Null when the chart has no Ascendant, so no rising sign is invented.

finalDispositors.description: Empty is a real result: every chain closed in a loop.
finalDispositors.title: Finaldispositors

state.description: domicile, exaltation, detriment, fall, peregrine or unrated. unrated is not peregrine: it marks a body the scheme assigns no rulership to at all, which is a different statement from a body that has dignities and is in none of them.

challenging.description: Zero or negative. Never netted against supportive.

contactCount.description: Coverage. A dimension with no contacts is not a zero -- zero means the geometry is neutral, absent means it is silent, and a pair with an unknown birth time is silent about everything the angles would have said.

finalDispositor.description: Null when the chain closes in a loop instead of a self-ruler.
finalDispositor.title: Finaldispositor

loop.description: The planets ruling each other's signs in a closed cycle. A chart can consist entirely of these and legitimately have no final dispositor anywhere.

components.description: The score broken into its parts. Published so a caller can see what made a planet dominant rather than being handed a number to trust; the weights themselves are in meta.dominantProfile.
components.title: Components

bodies.description: Bounded so one request cannot ask for thousands of lookups a row.
bodies.title: Bodies

max_rows.title: Max Rows

coRulers.description: Classical rulers displaced by the modern table. Reported, but not used to walk a dispositor chain, which needs a single next step.
coRulers.title: Corulers

Every house system the engine supports.

the two never drift, because an enum that silently lags the engine is worse
than none at all.

ambiguous.description: True at exactly 180 degrees, where the two midpoints are equally valid and the choice between them is arbitrary. Flagged rather than silently resolved.

NatalChartRequest.description:
Natal chart calculation request.

Preserves local civil date + optional local clock time + IANA timezone.
The engine owns historical timezone / DST interpretation — clients must not
pre-convert to UTC.

ayanamsa.description: Required when zodiac is sidereal, rejected otherwise. No default is applied: the schools disagree by over two degrees, which is enough to move a planet into the neighbouring sign, so choosing one is the caller's decision.

fold.description: Optional PEP 495 fold for ambiguous local times. Do not invent a fold; omit and surface AMBIGUOUS_LOCAL_TIME when unresolved.
fold.title: Fold

house_system.description: House system. Defaults to the engine calculation profile (western-modern-v1 → placidus). No silent fallback between systems.

local_date.description: Local civil birth date as YYYY-MM-DD.
local_date.title: Local Date

local_time.description: Local clock time as HH:MM or HH:MM:SS when birth time is known. Must be null when unknown_time is true.
local_time.title: Local Time

timezone.description: IANA timezone identifier (not a fixed UTC offset).
timezone.title: Timezone

unknown_time.description: When true, birth time is unknown. Angles/houses are omitted by the engine; local_time must be null.
unknown_time.title: Unknown Time

zodiac.description: Zodiac to report positions in. Defaults to tropical.

NatalChartRequest.title: NatalChartRequest

NatalChartResponse.description: The canonical natal chart, returned directly rather than in an envelope.

angles.description: Empty when the birth time is unknown. No substitute is used.
angles.title: Angles

houses.description: Empty when the birth time is unknown.
houses.title: Houses

NatalChartResponse.title: NatalChartResponse

available.description: Probed against the installed data files, not assumed.
available.title: Available

patterns.description: Empty is a common and correct result. Contained figures are suppressed: every grand cross holds two T-squares and every kite holds a grand trine.
patterns.title: Patterns

profile.description: The pattern profile, including every orb that decided a match.
profile.title: Profile

ReadinessResponse.description:
Whether the service can actually calculate, not merely whether it is up.

`/health` answering `ok` says the process is alive. It says nothing about
whether ephemeris data was provisioned, and a container missing that data
starts happily and then fails every chart request. This endpoint runs a real
calculation so a deploy fails at the readiness probe instead of in front of
users.
ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

timezone and DST interpretation stay with the engine on both sides.

topAspects.description: The highest-ranked contacts under the published ranking profile.

info.description: Thin HTTP adapter over the gbc-astro AstrologyEngine. All natal calculations are performed by the existing Python engine; this service does not reimplement astrology math, geocoding, persistence, or interpretation.
info.title: GetBirthChart Astrology API

get.description:
Probe the ephemeris provider with a real calculation.

`degraded` means optional bodies are unavailable -- typically Chiron without
`seas_18.se1` -- while the core chart still calculates. It is reported as
healthy so a partial provision does not take the service down, but it is
visible so it does not go unnoticed either.

200.description: Whether this instance can calculate a chart. Returns 503 when ephemeris data is missing or the provider dependency is absent.
Stelliums, grand trines, T-squares, grand crosses, yods and kites, with the widest leg orb of each.
Bodies, house systems and ayanamsas, with optional bodies probed rather than assumed. Ask here instead of discovering through an error.

get.summary: What this installation can actually calculate

200.description: Three totals -- supportive, challenging and activity -- with every contact that produced them. Deliberately not a percentage.

200.description: Canonical composite JSON: shortest-arc midpoint positions, with the methodology named under meta and any ambiguity reported in warnings.
Canonical Davison JSON: an ordinary chart for the midpoint moment and midpoint place of the two births, so its speeds, houses and applying/separating phases are real rather than constructed.
The node lands on exactly 0 degrees Aries by construction.

200.description: Every longitude multiplied by n. Aspects are recomputed, not carried over: collapsing an aspect family onto conjunctions is the technique.

Each row is exactly what a single-instant call returns; this is a convenience, not a second calculation path.
